purpose: Independent practice of A10.2 — comparing capacity. Used as Lesson 3 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can compare how much things hold.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compare how much things hold.
header.character_watermark: Max the Measure Moose in the top-right corner of the header, holding a measuring cup. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Circle the cup that holds more!
parts.student_instructions: Look at each pair. Circle the cup that HOLDS MORE.
parts.visual_layout: Five paired-cup rows stacked vertically. Each row shows two containers side by side: (1) bowl vs thimble, (2) bucket vs cup, (3) jug vs glass, (4) bathtub vs sink, (5) two same-size cups. Each pair ~3in × 1.5in.

image_placeholders.description: Five paired-container rows in B&W line art for a Kindergarten worksheet, each row ~3in × 1.5in. Each row shows two containers for capacity comparison. Row 1: large mixing bowl + tiny thimble. Row 2: full bucket + small cup. Row 3: tall jug + small drinking glass. Row 4: bathtub + small sink. Row 5: two identical drinking cups. Generous spacing for circling.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P1_PAIRS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to circle the container that holds more. Keywords name the containers shown.

parts.answer_key: Row 1: bowl. Row 2: bucket. Row 3: jug. Row 4: bathtub. Row 5: SAME — accept circling either or both.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Order the cups by capacity!
parts.student_instructions: Number the cups from 1 (holds least) to 4 (holds most).
parts.visual_layout: Four cups in a horizontal row, displayed in mixed order. Cup sizes: small, large, medium, tiny. Each cup ~1.5in tall. Beside each cup, a small numbered box for writing 1, 2, 3, or 4.

image_placeholders.description: Four cups arranged horizontally for a Kindergarten worksheet, in mixed-size order. From left to right: medium cup (~1.2in tall), tiny cup (~0.5in tall), large cup (~2in tall), small cup (~0.8in tall). All B&W line art with thin outlines. Beside each cup at its base, a small empty number box (~0.5in × 0.5in) for the child to write 1-4.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P2_CUPS at Part 2: instructions ask the child to order cups by capacity. Keywords name the visual elements (cups) and the comparison endpoints (least, most).

parts.answer_key: Left to right: medium→3, tiny→1, large→4, small→2.

parts.part_title: Part 3: Find more in your kitchen!
parts.student_instructions: Think about your kitchen at home. Pick 2 things that hold liquid. Draw them. Circle the one that HOLDS MORE.
parts.visual_layout: Two blank drawing boxes side by side, each ~3in × 2in with thin solid border. Below each box, a label line for the object's name.

image_placeholders.description: Two blank drawing boxes side by side for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each box is ~3in × 2in with a thin solid border. Below each box, a horizontal line for writing the object's name. Designed for the child to draw two kitchen containers and circle the one that holds more.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS03_P3_BOXES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to draw two kitchen containers. Keywords name the prompt focus (kitchen) and comparison criterion (more).

parts.answer_key: Any 2 kitchen liquid-holding containers. Common: pot vs cup, milk jug vs glass, bowl vs spoon, jug vs juice box.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, name 3 things at home that hold WATER.
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation artifact. Use Part 1 as the formative signal for height-capacity conflation — children who circle a tall thin container over a wide short one need the 'pour to find out' re-loop.
